description.en:
The alignment ontology of the AIAS information model. It joins the four subdomain patterns into one model of an AI application in an automated plant.

The four patterns stand on their own and import nothing from one another. Each rests on a standard, and each is usable without the others. This ontology is the only place where classes of different namespaces are related, which keeps a pattern free of everything it does not need.

It is built around the system elements of Haberfellner: a function transforms, a component is transformed or performs a transformation, and a relation ties the two together. What each subdomain contributes hangs below one of those three, so that a process step of VDI 3682 and an inference of ISO/IEC 22989 become comparable without either standard having to know about the other.

ALIGNMENT.md records every bridge this ontology builds, the reason for it and the strength it is stated at.

comments.en:
Nothing here is normative. The patterns rest on standards, this ontology rests on design decisions of this work, and every class and relation says which of the two it is.

Two classes are related with owl:equivalentClass, and only where the definitions are word for word the same. Control is one of them: ISO/IEC 22989, 3.5.5 and IEC 60050-351, 351-42-19 carry the identical wording and trace back to the same source, which makes the two the same concept rather than similar ones. Everything else is a subclass relation or a relation of its own, because an equivalence claims more than an overlap supports.

Two traps are recorded rather than resolved. Controllability appears in two patterns with the same spelling and different meanings, one a property of a dynamic system and one a property of an AI system, and they are deliberately not related. The actuator of IEC 60050-351 is the signal side driving a valve, not the valve, so the device class of this ontology matches the final controlling element instead. ALIGNMENT.md gives both in full.

note.value:
**Construct of this work**, equivalent to the technical resource of VDI 3682.

A resource is what a function is assigned to. Where its communication is described it also appears as an open system in the sense of ISO/IEC 7498-1, 4.1.3, which that pattern states on its own class.

**A subclass of the physical unit, not equivalent to it.** IEC 60050-351, 351-56-03 defines the physical unit as an item under consideration seen by construction, and every resource is one: VDI 3682 calls the technical resource a physical component of an automated plant. The reverse does not hold. A terminal block or a power supply is a physical unit and realises no transformation, so it is no technical resource, and an equivalence would be wrong in that direction.

The subclass axiom is what makes the chain from a device to its role in a control walkable. A model states a resource, the reasoner infers a physical unit, and the inverse relations of the IEC 60050-351 pattern lead from there through the functional units it realises to the action lines and the kind of path.

note.value:
IEC 60050-351, 351-42-19. The German term is Leiten, which covers both open-loop and closed-loop control as well as the supervisory tasks around them. National footnote N1 of that entry states this explicitly: control is the general term here, and the narrower Regeln and Steuern belong to the entries below.

No class for automating sits between this class and the two kinds of control. The standard defines automating in 351-43 as a task, alongside measuring and monitoring, not in 351-47 as a kind of control, and 351-42-31 treats the degree of automation as a proportion of the functions of a system. A hand-operated closed-loop control is a closed-loop control by 351-47-01 without being automated, so a subclass axiom would state more than the standard does. Whether a control runs by itself is recorded through the AI pattern, where automation is a function, and the two are related in the alignment.

comment.en: Purposeful action on or in a process to meet specified objectives.

note.value:
IEC 60050-351, 351-54-06, where the entry is stated for a process computer system.

Real time is a capability of a system with a stated interval, not a property of time itself. The pattern follows that reading, so a model states the capability and the interval separately rather than calling a duration real time.

IEC 60050-351, 351-47-06. The note to the entry states that a reset circuit, 351-47-62, has an open action although its structure has a closed action path.

This is the case that separates the pattern from the simplified reading that feedback alone makes a closed-loop control.

note.value:
ISO/IEC 22989, 3.3.5.

note.value:
ISO/IEC 7498-1, 5.3.1.14 to 5.3.1.16 define three kinds of data communication by direction: two-way simultaneous, two-way alternate, and one-way. The three are supplied as named individuals in ISO7498-instances.ttl.

The direction complements the source and target systems rather than repeating them. Which systems send and which receive follows from hasSourceSystem and hasTargetSystem; whether both directions are possible at once or only in turn does not, and that is what this class records. A Profibus segment carries data in both directions but one at a time, which makes it two-way alternate, while a full duplex Ethernet link is two-way simultaneous.

comment.en: The direction in which data communication takes place over a communication.

note.value: **Construct of this work.** The standard discusses evaluation without defining the measure it uses. A concrete metric is recorded as a named individual of this class.

comment.en: What an evaluation measures a model against, for example an F1 score or an error rate.

comment.en: Where data is acquired from, for example a sensor or a database.

note.value: Reified so that a value can be referred to and annotated, in the same arrangement and for the same reason as the quality of service value of the ISO 7498 pattern.

comment.en: The value a model assigns to one characteristic, together with its unit.

note.value: IEC 60050-351, 351-47-33. The definition names a real-time model of the process, which is the natural place for a data driven process model in a control structure.

comment.en: Closed-loop control which includes explicitly in its structure a real-time model of the process expressing the static and dynamic relationships between manipulated variables and controlled variables.

note.value:
VDI 3682 Part 1, Section 4.2.1 recommends modelling parallel process runs as a partially shared flow and explicitly requires no additional graphical elements for them. Introducing a class for the parallel flow is therefore a design decision of this pattern rather than an adoption from the standard.

A parallel flow states that a single connection belongs to a concurrent run. Grouping several connections into one conjunction is expressed through the dependency property between the states involved.

comment.en: A flow that is part of a partially shared flow denoting process steps running concurrently.

note.value: IEC 60050-351, 351-56-03. The building view: the device as it is bought and installed. Not disjoint with the functional unit, since the two are views rather than kinds.

comment.en: An item under consideration defined according to construction or configuration.

note.value: VDI 3682 Part 2, Section 5.1, after IEC 61360-1. It carries a unique ident, a long name, a short name, references to external identification systems, a version number and a revision number.

comment.en: The attribute uniquely identifying an object and its characteristics over the life cycle of a process description.

note.value: Named in note 2 to ISO/IEC 22989, 3.1.35, and discussed in clause 9, without an entry of its own.

comment.en: A task assigning inputs to discrete classes.

note.value:
IEC 60050-351, 351-47-02. Characteristic for open-loop control is the open action path, or in a closed action path the fact that the output variables being influenced by the input variables are not continuously or sequentially influencing themselves and not by the same input variables.

Deliberately **not** disjoint with closed-loop control: the standard admits open-loop control in a closed action path, so a disjointness axiom would contradict it. What separates the two is the action, not the path.

comment.en: A process whereby one or more variable quantities as input variables influence other variable quantities as output variables in accordance with the proper laws of the system.

note.value: ISO/IEC 22989, 3.5.11. Clause 6.2.2 asks stakeholders to assess risks across the whole life cycle, and this class is where a model records the result.

comment.en: The effect of uncertainty on objectives.

note.value: **Construct of this work.** The distinction from the external cloud is who operates it, which is what a data protection review turns on rather than any technical property.

comment.en: Computing infrastructure operated by the plant operator, away from the process but inside the organisation.

note.value: IEC 60050-351, 351-41-08. The entry states this through the state equation and the output equation; the wording here is the prose form of that.

comment.en: An element of the state vector of a system, from which together with the input variables the output variables are determined.

note.value: IEC 60050-351, 351-47-03. A closed path alone does not make a closed-loop control: see the open action, 351-47-06.

comment.en: An action path between the input variable and the output variable at which an additional action path goes back from the output variable to the input variable.

note.value: **Collecting class of this pattern.** The standard defines the dataset, 3.2.5, and the sample, 3.2.13, and grades data by its use, but names no class between the atom and the collection.

comment.en: A collection of samples an AI system acquires, processes or computes outputs for.

note.value: **Construct of this work.** A function running here leaves the organisation, which is what separates it from the internal cloud.

comment.en: Computing infrastructure operated by a third party.

note.value:
**Construct of this work**, after Haberfellner.

Relations are classes rather than object properties, so that a tie can carry properties of its own. An assignment is a thing a model annotates with a reason or a date, not an arrow between two boxes.

comment.en: A recorded tie between functions and components, or between components.

note.value:
**Collecting class of this work.** The standard describes the activities in clause 5.10 and clause 6.2 without naming a superclass for them.

Note that clause 8.3 of the standard uses the term AI function in a narrower sense, for computing a prediction alone. This class is broader on purpose, since a model has to record the whole life cycle rather than the operating step only.

comment.en: An activity in the life cycle of an AI system, transforming inputs into outputs.

note.value: IEC 60050-351, 351-49-03. The summing point of Figure 2, and the place where a closed action path returns.

comment.en: A functional unit that forms the control difference variable from the reference variable and the feedback variable.

note.value: **Collecting class of this pattern.** The standard defines the qualities of clause 3.5 without naming what they have in common. Named individuals are supplied in ISO22989-instances.ttl.

comment.en: A named property of an AI system to which a model assigns a value, such as robustness or reliability.

note.value: IEC 60050-351, 351-48-06, marked m in Figures 1 and 2.

comment.en: The output variable of the controlling element, which is the input variable of the actuator.

note.value: VDI 3682 Part 1, Section 4.2.2 models alternative process runs as separate flows, again without additional graphical elements. Introducing a class for the alternative flow is a design decision of this pattern. Where alternative flows are present, the system limit must not be used as a balance limit.

comment.en: A flow that is part of a separate flow denoting mutually exclusive process paths.

note.value: ISO/IEC 7498-1, 7.4.4 names throughput, transit delay, residual error rate, and establishment delay among the parameters of the transport service. Named individuals for these are supplied in ISO7498-instances.ttl, where the list stays open, since a model may need parameters the standard does not enumerate.

comment.en: A named characteristic of a communication, such as throughput or transit delay, that a quality of service statement assigns a value to.

note.value: IEC 60050-351, 351-47-15. Its sampling period, 351-47-16, is the normative equivalent of what practice calls cycle time, a term the standard does not define.

comment.en: Closed-loop control in which the input variables of the controlling system are taken discontinuously in time to generate new values of the manipulated variable, which are updated discontinuously and maintained by holding elements between updates.

note.value: IEC 60050-351, 351-49-06. The outermost frame of Figures 1 and 2, covering an open-loop and a closed-loop control alike.

comment.en: A functional unit consisting of the controlling system and the controlled system.
Machine learning that makes use of both labelled and unlabelled data during training.
A variable quantity which represents the controlled variable and is returned to the comparing element.

note.value: VDI 3682 Part 1, Section 4.1. Information leaving a process is the point of contact with the communication pattern of the AIAS information model.

comment.en: Information required by a process operator to carry out its transformation, or information created by it.

note.value: **Collecting class of this pattern.** The standard defines the four kinds below, 3.3.9, 3.3.11, 3.3.12 and 3.3.17, and discusses them in clause 5.11, but names no common superclass.

comment.en: The kind of machine learning an algorithm performs.

note.value: **Construct of this work.** ISO/IEC 22989 describes evaluation in clause 5.10 without naming a procedure for it.

comment.en: The procedure assessing a model against an evaluation metric.

note.value: IEC 60050-351, 351-48-01. Only a closed-loop control has one: it is what is measured and compared with the reference variable.

comment.en: The output variable of the controlled system that will be acted upon by one or more manipulated variables.

note.value:
IEC 60050-351, 351-49-07.

The German term is Steller, and the entry is the signal side of the manipulating equipment, not the element acting on the flow. That element is the final controlling element, 351-49-08. The common rendering of the German Aktor as actuator conflates the two and would put the wrong class on a valve.

comment.en: A functional unit that generates the manipulated variable, required to drive the final controlling element, from the output variable of the controlling element.

note.value: **Construct of this work.** Clause 8.6.2 of ISO/IEC 22989 discusses edge computing without defining a device for it. What makes a device an edge device here is where it sits, not what it is built from.

comment.en: A resource with computing capacity placed near the process it serves.

note.value: Discussed in ISO/IEC 22989, clause 9.2, without an entry of its own.

comment.en: A task producing new outputs, such as text, images or audio, from learned representations.

note.value:
Addition of this pattern, not a class of ISO/IEC 7498-1. Clause 1.3 states that the fact a system is open implies no particular systems implementation, technology or means of interconnection, so the standard names none.

An engineering model has to record which protocol is used, which is why the class exists. Named individuals such as Ethernet, TCP, or MQTT are supplied in ISO7498-instances.ttl, each related to the layer it realises. Whether a given technology fits the layer a model claims for it is a question for the rule base of the modelling assistance, not an axiom of this pattern.

comment.en: A concrete protocol or transmission technique realising the services of a layer.

note.value:
IEC 60050-351, 351-49-05, where the full term is measuring element in control technology.

Not the same entry as the sensing element, 351-56-26. The sensing element responds to the measurand, whereas this element produces the feedback variable that closes the action path. A model may realise both through one physical unit.

comment.en: A functional unit that forms the feedback variable at its output from the controlled variable applied to its input.

note.value: IEC 60050-351, 351-56-02. The functional view: what something does, irrespective of how it is built.

comment.en: An item under consideration defined according to function or effect.
An input variable to a comparing element in a controlling system, which sets the desired value of the controlled variable and is deducted from the command variable.

note.value:
ISO/IEC 22989, 3.3.4, which defines it as a characteristic of a machine learning algorithm affecting its learning process, selected prior to training.

This pattern places it on the algorithm superclass, so that a model algorithm and an evaluation algorithm may carry one as well: the number of layers of a network, or the threshold of a rule. Applying the entry beyond machine learning is a reading of it rather than the entry itself, and a rule threshold recorded here is such a case.

comment.en: A characteristic of an algorithm that affects its behaviour, chosen in advance rather than determined by training.

note.value: IEC 60050-351, 351-47-42. The automatic modification is what a learning system performs online.

comment.en: Closed-loop control with automatic modification of the structure or parameters of the controlling system to compensate for varying operating conditions and states.

note.value: IEC 60050-351, 351-41-01. The standard notes that the short form quantity is often used for it.

comment.en: A physical quantity the value of which is subject to change and which can usually be measured.
Closed-loop control in which the control algorithm is expressed by fuzzy logic using facts, inference rules and quantifiers based on experience and intuition.

note.value: IEC 60050-351, 351-57-06. The standard defines no safety integrity level; IEC 61508 does.

comment.en: The part of the overall safety that depends on functional and physical units operating correctly in response to their inputs.

note.value: IEC 60050-351, 351-42-22. The formal precondition for any application that intervenes in a process.

comment.en: The property of a system implying that its state variables may be changed from an initial state into a desired final state within a finite time interval, via proper time variations of the input variables.

note.value: **Construct of this work.**

comment.en: A general purpose computing resource within the plant.

note.value: IEC 60050-351, 351-47-45. The deviation from the properties assumed for the design is what a data driven model faces as a shift of its operating conditions.

comment.en: Closed-loop control able to keep system properties within a prescribed area even if the properties of the controlled system or of the controller deviate from those assumed for the design.

note.value: **Construct of this work.** The counterpart of the data source.

comment.en: Where data is stored, for example a database or a cloud service.

note.value: IEC 60050-351, 351-49-01. The German terms are Regelstrecke and Steuerstrecke, so the class covers the plant side of both kinds of control.

comment.en: A functional unit which is to be influenced according to the control task.

note.value:
IEC 60050-351, 351-49-09. The German term is Stelleinrichtung, drawn as the dashed grouping in Figures 1 and 2.

It groups the signal side, 351-49-07, and the element acting on the flow, 351-49-08, which the standard otherwise keeps apart. Membership is recorded through consistsOfUnit rather than through a subclass axiom, since the two parts stay units in their own right.

comment.en: A functional unit consisting of the actuator and the final controlling element.
A variable quantity which is acting on a system from the outside and which is independent of the other variable quantities of the system.

note.value: IEC 60050-351, 351-47-20. The standard states no genus beyond control, so the class sits under Control. Storage-programmable logic control, 351-47-22, is a kind of this, which is how the standard covers what practice calls a programmable logic controller.

comment.en: Control the functions of which are defined by a program that was previously entered.

note.value: ISO/IEC 7498-1, 5.2.1.11. Entities in the same layer are termed peer entities, 5.2.1.3, which this pattern expresses through the peerEntity relation rather than a separate class.

comment.en: An active element within a subsystem embodying a set of capabilities defined for the layer.

note.value: Reified so that a value can be annotated and referred to, in the same way and for the same reason as the flow of the VDI 3682 pattern. The parameter it belongs to is a named individual, the value and unit are literals of this model.

comment.en: The value a quality of service statement assigns to one parameter, together with its unit.

note.value: ISO/IEC 7498-1, 5.3 and 6.4. A connection is established before data transfer and released afterwards, so the transfer can rely on state held for its duration.

comment.en: A communication established, held, and released as a connection between the participating entities.

note.value: IEC 60050-351, 351-42-24. Behaviour, not structure.

comment.en: The influence of one variable quantity on another variable quantity.

note.value: IEC 60050-351, 351-47-58. The standard assigns this to closed-loop control explicitly, so the pattern follows rather than leaving it open.

comment.en: Closed-loop control in which the control algorithm explicitly incorporates one or more sets of rules.

note.value: Described in ISO/IEC 22989, clause 5.10, without an entry of its own. What it consists of is recorded through the data process steps.

comment.en: The function transforming input data into output data.

note.value: Named in note 2 to ISO/IEC 22989, 3.1.35, and discussed in clause 5.11.2, without an entry of its own.

comment.en: A task identifying groups of similar samples.
A set of interrelated elements considered in a defined context as a whole and separated from their environment.

note.value:
ISO/IEC 22989, 3.1.2.

The class is what a model needs as soon as one system carries more than one approach. A system combining a learned classifier with a rule-based decision has two components, each performing its own functions, and without them the two would be indistinguishable.

comment.en: A functional element that constructs an AI system.

note.value:
ISO/IEC 22989, 3.1.27.

Note 2 to the entry states that prediction does not necessarily refer to predicting something in the future, and note 1 that predictions can be followed by further outputs such as recommendations, decisions and actions.

comment.en: The primary output of an AI system when provided with input data or information.
An atomic data element processed in quantities by a machine learning algorithm or an AI system.

note.value: IEC 60050-351, 351-48-05, marked e in Figure 2. It exists only where a comparison takes place, which is why it appears in the closed-loop figure alone.

comment.en: The difference between the reference variable and the feedback variable.

note.value: IEC 60050-351, 351-56-24. A note to the entry includes the process control station and the operating manuals, which is how the standard covers what practice calls a control room.

comment.en: The entirety of devices and programs used for the task of controlling, and in a broader sense all instructions and programs used for it.

note.value:
**Not a term of the standard.** IEC 60050-351 draws this unit at the right-hand edge of Figures 1 and 2, where x enters and q leaves the control system, but gives it no entry, no number and no index line. A search of the full text finds the wording only inside the two figures.

The class is nevertheless kept, because the final controlled variable it produces is a term of the standard, 351-48-10, and without a unit for it that variable would have no origin in a model. The last step of both figures would then go unrecorded.

Anyone aligning this pattern with another should treat the class as a construct of this work rather than as normative vocabulary. REFERENCE.md lists it under the elements taken from the figures instead of from the entries.

label.en: Generation of the Final Controlled Variable

comment.en: A functional unit that forms the final controlled variable from the controlled variable.
A collection of data with a shared format.

note.value: **Construct of this work**, matching the product of VDI 3682. Products and resources share the component level and differ in their role: a resource performs functions, a product is transformed by them.

comment.en: A physical component that a function transforms, produces or consumes.
The process to select a subset of data samples intended to present patterns and trends similar to that of the larger dataset.

note.value:
**Construct of this work**, after the system elements of Haberfellner.

The class is what makes the alignment work. A process operator of VDI 3682 transforms products, an inference of ISO/IEC 22989 derives a conclusion, and a control of IEC 60050-351 acts on a process. In their own standards the three have nothing in common. Below this class they are assigned to a resource through one mechanism, and a question asking what a device does answers with all of them.

comment.en: A purposeful transformation, turning inputs into outputs to meet an objective of the system.

note.value: Grouping of this pattern, covering overshoot and the stability margins.

comment.en: A characteristic expressing how well a control performs, rather than how long it takes.
An action path between the input variable and the output variable at which no action path goes back from the output variable to the input variable.
The process of attaching a set of descriptive information to data without any change to that data.

note.value:
ISO/IEC 22989, 3.5.5, which takes the definition from IEC 61800-7-1:2015, 3.2.6.

**The wording is identical to IEC 60050-351, 351-42-19**, and both trace back to the same source. The two are therefore the same concept rather than merely similar ones, and the alignment relates them with owl:equivalentClass. This pattern states nothing about the other, since referencing another namespace would drag it along wherever this pattern is used.

comment.en: Purposeful action on or in a process to meet specified objectives.
An object under consideration defined according to function and scope.

note.value: VDI 3682 Part 1, Section 4.1. The system limit must not be used as a balance limit when alternative process runs are described.

comment.en: The boundary determining the observation horizon of a process. Under certain conditions it may also be regarded as a balance limit for incoming and outgoing products and energies.

note.value: **Construct of this work.** Described in ISO/IEC 22989, clause 5.10 and clause 6.2.8, without an entry. It is what evaluation data, 3.2.14, exists for.

comment.en: The function assessing the performance of a final model before it is deployed.

note.value: ISO/IEC 7498-1, 5.6.1.3. Figure 9 shows that a protocol data unit of one layer becomes a service data unit of the layer below, which is the encapsulation the mapsToServiceDataUnit relation expresses.

comment.en: A unit of data specified in a protocol, consisting of protocol control information and possibly user data.

note.value: ISO/IEC 7498-1, 4.1.3. A real system complying with the requirements of the OSI standards in its communication with other real systems is a real open system, 4.1.2. In the AIAS information model a technical resource of the plant appears as an open system when its communication is described.

comment.en: The representation of those aspects of a real system that are pertinent to open systems interconnection.

note.value:
**Construct of this work**, derived from ISO/IEC 22989, 3.1.23 and 3.3.7.

It is what a model is before its parameters are known. The distinction matters because the same architecture trained on different data yields different models, and a model records which of the two it is talking about.

A concrete architecture is recorded as a named individual of this class rather than as a subclass, which keeps the pattern independent of libraries and methods.

comment.en: The procedure describing the structure of a model, such as the architecture of a neural network or a set of rules.

note.value: VDI 3682 Part 1, Section 4.1.

comment.en: Things of the real world that are transformed within a technical process. The generic term also covers flows of materials and substances.

note.value:
IEC 60050-351, 351-49-08. The German term is Stellglied, and a valve is the typical case.

The standard places it inside the controlled system. This pattern records that through the relation partOfControlledSystem rather than through a subclass axiom, so another pattern may hold the same valve as a resource executing a process operation without the two contradicting each other.

comment.en: A functional unit forming part of the controlled system and arranged at its input, driven by the manipulated variable and manipulating the mass flow or energy flow.

note.value:
ISO/IEC 22989, 3.3.15.

The entry names all three ingredients: an algorithm, training data and the parameters that come out. A training missing any of them is not one, which is what makes this function the place where the difference between an algorithm and a model arises.

comment.en: The process to determine or to improve the parameters of a machine learning model, based on a machine learning algorithm, by using training data.

note.value: IEC 60050-351, 351-47-01. Characteristic for closed-loop control is the closed action in which the controlled variable continuously or sequentially influences itself in the action path of the closed loop. The closed action is required, not merely a closed path.

comment.en: A process whereby one variable quantity, namely the controlled variable, is continuously or sequentially measured, compared with another variable quantity, namely the reference variable, and influenced in such a manner as to adjust to the reference variable.

note.value:
ISO/IEC 22989, 3.1.17. Note 1 to the entry states that in AI a premise is either a fact, a rule, a model, a feature or raw data, which is why both a symbolic and a subsymbolic system perform inference.

Note 2 adds that the term refers both to the process and its result. This pattern uses it for the process and records the result as a prediction, 3.1.27.

comment.en: Reasoning by which conclusions are derived from known premises.
A set of elements or systems incorporated in the closed action of a closed-loop control.

note.value: ISO/IEC 22989, 3.5.18. Clause 6.2.4 treats validation together with verification as one stage of the life cycle. Validation asks whether the right system was built, verification whether the system was built right.

comment.en: Confirmation, through the provision of objective evidence, that the requirements for a specific intended use or application have been fulfilled.

note.value: IEC 60050-351, 351-47-12. The arrangement of an open-loop control, as against the loop of a closed-loop control.

comment.en: A set of elements or systems which act upon one another in a series structure.

note.value: VDI 3682 Part 2, Figure 2 carries state as a class of the information model. Part 1, Section 4.1 deliberately avoids the term in the graphical notation because it is considered ambiguous there, and works with product, energy and information directly. This pattern follows Part 2.

comment.en: The condition of a product, an energy or an information at a given point of a process, either as the status ante operationem before a transformation or as the status post operationem after it.
A fault that inhibits alterations of the output variables of the control equipment although all program-defined conditions for such alterations are fulfilled.

note.value:
**Construct of this work.** ISO/IEC 22989 defines the machine learning algorithm, 3.3.6, but no general algorithm and no superclass for the kinds below.

The class exists so that the hyperparameter, 3.3.4, has one place to attach to. The standard defines the hyperparameter for the machine learning algorithm, whereas a model algorithm and an evaluation algorithm carry one as well, for example the number of layers of a network or the threshold of a metric.

comment.en: A parameterisable mathematical procedure, described apart from any execution of it.

note.value:
VDI 3682 Part 1, Figure 3 lists the flow as one of the eight symbols of the graphical notation, where it is an edge rather than an object.

Reifying the flow as a class is a design decision of this pattern and deviates from the VDI 3682 ODP of Helmut Schmidt University, which models flows as object properties. The reification is required because the AIAS alignment ontology treats flows as instances of Relation so that the modelling assistance can annotate them, and because the graphical notation of this work carries a class field and a naming field inside every symbol, which an edge cannot hold.

The direct properties hasInput and hasOutput are retained and inferred from the reified flows through property chains, so that reasoning over predecessor and successor is unaffected by the reification.

comment.en: A directed connection transporting a product, an energy or an information between a state and a process operator.

note.value: ISO/IEC 22989, 3.3.6. The only algorithm the standard defines. What kind of learning it performs is recorded through basedOnLearning.

comment.en: An algorithm to determine parameters of a machine learning model from data according to given criteria.

note.value: IEC 60050-351, 351-42-35. The technical process pattern has no class for the plant as a whole, only for its individual resources, so this fills a gap rather than duplicating one.

comment.en: A complete set of technical equipment and facilities for solving a defined technical task.

note.value: Reified so that a value can be referred to and annotated with its source or the conditions it holds under, in the same arrangement and for the same reason as the characteristic value of the IEC 60050-351 pattern.

comment.en: The value a model assigns to one characteristic, together with its unit.

note.value: IEC 60050-351, 351-42-31. May be given only for a defined system whose limits are specified. Full automatic operation means all functions except switching on and off are automated.

comment.en: The proportion of automatic functions to the entire set of functions of a system or plant.

note.value:
IEC 60050-351, 351-49-04. The German terms are Steuerglied and Regelglied, one entry for both.

The entry is the element that appears in Figure 1 as well as in Figure 2, which is why the same class serves an open-loop and a closed-loop control. What differs is the variable at its input, not the unit.

comment.en: A functional unit that forms its output variable from the command variable in open-loop control and from the control difference variable in closed-loop control.

note.value: Addition of this pattern, connecting the reference model of clause 6 to the data units of 5.6.

comment.en: Relates a communication to a data unit conveyed over it.

note.value: ISO/IEC 22989, 3.1.35. A system may address more than one task, which is why this is not functional.

comment.en: Relates an AI system to a task it addresses.

note.value: ISO/IEC 22989, 3.3.4. Placed on the algorithm superclass, so a model algorithm and an evaluation algorithm may carry one as well.

comment.en: Relates an algorithm to a characteristic chosen in advance that affects its behaviour.

note.value: IEC 60050-351, 351-43. Mapping an application onto the tasks the standard names keeps a model connected to existing plant documentation.

comment.en: Relates an item under consideration to a function of control technology it performs.

note.value: IEC 60050-351, 351-47-04 and 351-47-06 both define the action with respect to a path. Functional: one action belongs to one path.

comment.en: Relates an action to the action path it takes place over.
The numeric quantity of a quality of service value.

note.value: ISO/IEC 22989, 3.1.27 defines the prediction as the primary output of an AI system when provided with input data.

comment.en: Relates an inference to the prediction it produces.

note.value: The property 3.3.12 and 3.3.17 turn on. Stated on the data rather than derived from the presence of labels, so that a model can record the intent before the labels exist.

comment.en: Whether the samples of a dataset carry labels.

note.value: Functional: one value quantifies exactly one characteristic.

comment.en: Relates a characteristic value to the characteristic it quantifies.

note.value: Which kind of data belongs to which function follows from the entries: 3.3.16 for training, 3.2.15 for validation, 3.2.14 for evaluation and 3.2.12 for inference in operation.

comment.en: Relates a function to the data it works on.

note.value: IEC 60050-351, 351-48-01. Only closed-loop control has one, since the controlled variable is what is measured and compared.

comment.en: Relates a closed-loop control to the controlled variable it acts upon.

note.value: **Construct of this work**, after ISO/IEC 22989, clause 8.6.1. One of the two relations reaching outside the AI system.

comment.en: Relates an acquisition to where the data comes from.

note.value: ISO/IEC 22989, 3.3.15 defines training as the process determining or improving the parameters. This relation is that determining, and it is what turns an algorithm into a model.

comment.en: Relates a training to the model parameters it determines.

note.value: VDI 3682 Part 2, Figure 5.

comment.en: The name of a characteristic.

note.value: A literal rather than a reference to a unit ontology, so that the pattern stays free of further imports. Several qualities are dimensionless, in which case a model leaves this out.

comment.en: The unit of a characteristic value, where the characteristic has one.
The numeric quantity of a characteristic value.

note.value: Super property of the role specific relations below, so that a model may record a variable before its role is settled.

comment.en: Relates an automation or a system to a variable quantity involved in it.

note.value:
ISO/IEC 7498-1, 6.5.1.1 calls an open system that is the ultimate source or destination of data an end system. Source here means the origin of the data, that is the sending system, which is the reading the standard uses throughout.

Direction follows from how the two properties are filled rather than from a separate statement. A system named as source alone sends, one named as target alone receives, and one named on both sides both sends and receives, which is what makes a communication bidirectional. A bus segment names its master as source and its slaves as targets.

comment.en: Relates a communication to an open system data flows from.

note.value: ISO/IEC 22989, 3.3.9 to 3.3.17. Functional: an algorithm performs one kind of learning, which negative model 03 tests.

comment.en: Relates a machine learning algorithm to the kind of learning it performs.

note.value: VDI 3682 Part 2, Figure 5 and Figure 7.

comment.en: The relation establishing part of a characteristic.

note.value: ISO/IEC 22989, 3.2.10. Whether data carries labels is what separates supervised learning, 3.3.12, from unsupervised learning, 3.3.17.

note.value:
VDI 3682 states the assignment from the process operator: hasAssignment runs from the process operator to the assignment, and assignedResource from there to the resource. Both follow the guideline, and neither reaches a function that is not a process operator.

This relation closes that gap. It says which function an assignment carries, whatever subdomain the function comes from, and it is what makes the common function level usable rather than merely stated. Without it a model could group a process operator and an inference under one superclass and still have no way to assign the second to a device.

Deliberately not a superproperty of hasAssignment. The two run in opposite directions, from the function and from the assignment, and relating them would require an inverse the pattern does not state.

comment.en: Relates an assignment to the function it assigns to a resource.

note.value:
The bridge between the communication subdomain and the AI subdomain, and a relation rather than an equivalence on purpose.

Setting the data of the two subdomains equal does not hold. ISO/IEC 7498-1, 5.6.1.2 defines user data as the payload of one transmission, ISO/IEC 22989 defines data as a collection of samples, and the two differ in what determines them and in how many of them there are. A ping carries payload with no dataset involved, and a training dataset exists whether or not it is ever transmitted.

Keeping them apart is what makes a question answerable: which communications carry a given dataset, on which layer and with which quality of service. Under an equivalence the dataset would be the payload of one transmission, and the question would be meaningless.

comment.en: Relates the payload of a transmission to the dataset it carries.

note.value: IEC 60050-351 states a formula symbol for most characteristics of 351-45 and 351-46, which makes a model checkable against the figures of the standard.

note.value:
Adopted from the VDI 3682 ODP of Helmut Schmidt University and not contained in the standard itself.

Under the open world assumption several inputs of one process operator always denote alternatives. Where inputs are required jointly, this has to be stated explicitly. The property acts as a conjunction between states, so that an expression such as "A and B, or C and D" becomes representable: dependency is asserted between A and B and between C and D.

The property complements ParallelFlow. A parallel flow qualifies a single connection, whereas dependency groups several connections into one conjunction.

comment.en: Expresses that two states are required together rather than as alternatives to one another.

IEC 60050-351, 351-56-02 and 351-56-03 define the two as views of one item under consideration, taken by function and by construction.

The relation is the axis the technical process pattern lacks, where a technical resource is atomic. One physical unit may realise several functional units and one functional unit may be spread over several physical units, so no cardinality is asserted.

ISO/IEC 7498-1, Figure 9 and its note 3: a protocol data unit of a layer may be mapped one to one into a service data unit of the layer below, though other relationships are possible.

This is the encapsulation that recurs down the layers, and it is what makes the practice terms frame, packet, and segment unnecessary as classes: each is the protocol data unit of a particular layer, and the relation states how one becomes the payload of the next.

comment.en: Relates a protocol data unit of one layer to the service data unit of the layer below that carries it.

note.value: Functional: one value quantifies exactly one parameter.

comment.en: Relates a quality of service value to the parameter it quantifies.

comment.en: A reference from an object to an external identification system such as AKZ, KKS or NE 100.

note.value:
IEC 60050-351, 351-49-08 places the final controlling element inside the controlled system.

Stated as a relation rather than a subclass axiom on purpose. VDI 3682 would hold the same valve as a technical resource executing a process operation, and a subclass axiom here would make the two readings contradict. As a relation both stand.

note.value:
ISO/IEC 7498-1, 4.1.3 defines the open system as the representation of those aspects of a real system that are pertinent to open systems interconnection. A thing is not an open system in itself, it is one under that view, which is why this is a relation rather than a subclass axiom.

The domain is the component rather than the resource. A product may take part in a communication as well: a workpiece carrying an RFID tag or a barcode is read along the line, and narrowing this to resources would rule that out.

The ISO 7498 pattern already states the intent on its own class. This relation is what a model uses to record it.

comment.en: Relates a component to the open system it appears as when its communication is described.
Relates a signal to a parameter of it that represents information.

note.value: The step from the function to what it actually does, so that a model can record an order of preparation rather than one opaque activity.
